title: DFS in Reykjavik: Chase the Path!
description: Watch Depth-First Search (DFS) explore Reykjavik’s streets like a backtracking detective. The frontier dives deep, then retraces steps until it finds the route—no shortcuts, just pure graph traversal.
ig_caption:
🌍🧭 **DFS in Reykjavik (Miðborg)** — follow the deep dive! 🇮🇸

In this visualization, **Depth-First Search (DFS)** treats the street network as a **graph**: intersections are **nodes**, and road segments are **edges**. DFS keeps a stack (explicit or via recursion) and **goes as deep as possible** along one branch before backtracking—classic **graph search with backtracking**. 🧠🔁

On real street maps, DFS can be fast to traverse connected regions, but it’s not guaranteed to find the *shortest* path unless the graph structure and neighbor ordering cooperate. That’s why neighbor ordering + traversal strategy matter in practice. ⚙️📍

✅ Want the next episode on comparing **DFS vs BFS** on the same map? Comment your pick—and **save + share** this reel with a coding friend! 🚀💬
fb_caption:
Reykjavik’s street grid becomes a graph, and **DFS (Depth-First Search)** explores it by diving deep and backtracking when it hits dead ends. 📍🧠 This is a real-world way to understand graph search mechanics: nodes/intersections, edges/roads, and traversal order shaping what you find.

Perfect for students learning **pathfinding algorithms**, **graph theory**, and **coding interviews**.
